siding_exposure_m.note: INVENTED WITHIN A STOCK SET, NOT DERIVED. No source states the exposed face of any Chicago building's siding. The value is one of four period mill sidings — 4.5, 5, 5.5 or 6 in to the weather; this roof wears 6 in — dealt in this building's own parcel recipe: drawn from the set on this record's stable key, then advanced so that no roof of the parcel standing within 60 m hangs the same course. It is NOT keyed to a construction season the way the named buildings' stocks are: this record's 1835-01-01 is the programme's count-unit convention and not a date anything was built, so keying to it would deal every anonymous roof in the town one stock. The separation is the surface variety T-0049 reconstructs, not a claim about 1835. docs/LIBERTIES.md L148 owns the invention and the recipe half is recorded beside it, under `tools/siding_stock.py`.

residents.name: The lodgers of Reconstructed H1 small boarding house #007
residents.why: THE BED IS THE CLAIM. The lodging model puts 7 people in this house on an ordinary night and 17 when it was full, apportioned from the town model's own bracket. These people are here because the beds are, and for no other reason.
residents.basis: A CONTAINER, NOT A FAMILY. `data/residents/` cannot carry a person outside a household, and the people who boarded in one house were not kin. This record holds the beds of one house and claims no relation between the people in them beyond the roof.

persons.name: Esther Bardwell
persons.note: RECONSTRUCTED, NOT FOUND. Nobody is named by any source here. This roof is itself a reconstruction of the 1835 building programme, raised as a lodging place, and a lodging place with no keeper is not one. The whole of what is claimed is that: an adult of this sex and band kept this invented house. A NAMED house is never given a keeper this way — see the tool's refusals. The family this keeper is owed is not drawn here; `household_owed` says which ticket owes it. No figure is drawn (L1).

citations.citation: Chicago · July 1835: Building Inventory and Architectural Reconstruction Specification. Prepared for Kevin Haas, August 2026.
what_it_supplies: A 665-roof production target with independently reconcilable group, district, level, and construction totals.
Thirty-five architectural family definitions with dimensional and massing bands.
District character, spacing, variation, finish, and chronology constraints for a July 1835 reconstruction.
A required distinction between named documentary landmarks and anonymous inferred infill.
what_it_does_not_supply: A surviving July 1835 building census or parcel-by-parcel roof register.
Exact locations, dimensions, appearance, occupants, or construction dates for anonymous roofs.
Authority to replace stronger building-specific evidence already represented in the dataset.

research_note: RECONSTRUCTED / GENERATED, NOT AN ATTESTED NAMED BUILDING. Aggregate mix follows the supplied specification; exact presence, position, footprint, finish and instance-level form are interpretive. H-family boarding-house massing currently uses a generic frame dwelling/block archetype.

lodging.note: The town model puts a boarding house at 9 people on an ordinary night and 21 when full, from the 1840 household tail (p90 and p99 of 964 Chicago households). This building takes the share of its class's total that its 119 m² of enclosed floor (79 m² × 1.5 storeys) is of the class's floor area.
lodging.replaceable_by: Any source that states this house's rooms, beds or lodgers on a dated day: an advertisement counting its rooms, a traveller's account of how many it slept, a licence return. A stated capacity retires the apportioned one outright.

occupancy.statement: 7 on this card against an ordinary night's 7 beds: 3 seated here from elsewhere in the layer, where no source gives them a roof, 3 drawn against the order book's lodging buckets for beds that were standing empty, a keeper drawn for a roof this programme raised.
occupancy.keeper_owed: Minted by this stage as a solitary keeper. The family a keeper is owed is `family/none` in the order book and belongs to T-1171 and T-1174.
